# Scatter plot of Rosetta (CartesianDDG) $\Delta \Delta$G prediction vs. experimental melting temperature ($\Delta T_m$)

Rosetta $\Delta \Delta$G is calculated by subtracting the predicted Rosetta energy of the native state structure from the predicted energy of the mutated structure. In Rosetta, the more stable a protein is, the smaller its estimated energy is. Therefore, more negative values of $\Delta \Delta$G reflect stabilising mutations whereas more positive values of $\Delta \Delta$G signify destabilising mutations. The authors of the CartesianDDG protocol (https://doi.org/10.3389/fbioe.2020.558247) note that "[a] mutation is classified as stabilizing if the change in free energy is ≤-1 kcal/mol, it is classified as destabilizing if the change is ≥1 kcal/mol, and neutral if it falls between these values". 

Plotting scatter plot of Rosetta CartesianDDG $\Delta \Delta$G predictions and $\Delta T_m$ values

```{r, fig.align = 'center'}
cartesianDDG_plot <- ggplot(mutations_df, aes(x = -ddG, y = delta_tm, color = protein)) +
  geom_point(aes(fill=protein), size=0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, aes(fill=protein), alpha=0.2, size = 0.7) +
  scale_color_manual(values = color_list) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = color_list) + 
  theme_light() +
  theme(text=element_text(family="Times New Roman", size=12), plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) + 
  labs(title = expression(paste("Rosetta (CartesianDDG): ", Delta*T[m], " vs. predicted ΔΔG")),
       y = expression(paste(Delta*T[m], " (\u00B0C)")), 
       x = expression(paste(-Delta*Delta*G, " (kcal/mol)")), 
       color= "Protein", 
       fill="Protein")

print(cartesianDDG_plot)
```

Checking whether the two variables are statistically dependent on each other

```{r}
# Study relationship between delta_tm and DDG using a linear mixed effects model
# Account for differing intercepts using protein as a random effect
ddg_delta_tm_model <- lmerTest::lmer(delta_tm ~ -ddG + (1|protein), data = mutations_df)

# Print model summary to check significance
summary(ddg_delta_tm_model)
```

Based on these results, Rosetta CartesianDDG $\Delta \Delta$G predictions and experimental $\Delta T_m$ measurements do not display a statistically significant relationship. 

# Scatter plot of DynaMut2 $\Delta \Delta$G prediction vs. experimental melting temperature ($\Delta T_m$)

DynaMut2 $\Delta \Delta$G predictions have the opposite sign compared to those of Rosetta, as negative $\Delta \Delta$G values signify destabilizing mutations and vice versa. Unlike in Rosetta CartesianDDG, the authors of DynaMut2 do not provide specific boundaries for predicted $\Delta \Delta$G values that are used to classify mutations to neutral, stabilizing and destabilizing. Moreover, DynaMut2 can only handle up to 3 mutations at once. Therefore, not all mutations were studied using the tool as they had more than 3 simultaneous mutations. The tree excluded mutations were:

* Brazzein_ST0103 - 7 mutations
* MNEI_ST0134 - 4 mutations
* MNEI_ST0136 - 7 mutations

```{r}

```

Checking whether the two variables are statistically dependent on each other

```{r}
# Study relationship between delta_tm and DDG using a linear mixed effects model
# Account for differing intercepts using protein as a random effect
dynamut_delta_tm_model <- lmerTest::lmer(delta_tm ~ dynamut2_prediction + (1|protein), data = mutations_df)

# Print model summary to check significance
summary(dynamut_delta_tm_model)
```

Based on these results, DynaMut2 $\Delta \Delta$G predictions and experimental $\Delta T_m$ measurements do not display a statistically significant relationship. 

# Checking the relationship between DynaMut2 and Rosetta CartesianDDG predictions

As neither of the two tools seemed to correlate well with the experimental values, it could still be that the predictions correlate with each other. 

```{r, fig.align = 'center'}
ddgs_scatterplot <- ggplot(mutations_df, aes(x = dynamut2_prediction, y = -ddG, color = protein)) +
  geom_point(aes(fill=protein), size=0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, aes(fill=protein), alpha=0.2, size = 0.7) +
  scale_color_manual(values = color_list) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = color_list) + 
  theme_light() +
  geom_vline(xintercept=0, alpha=0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept=-1, alpha=0.25) +
  geom_hline(yintercept=0, alpha=0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept=1, alpha=0.25) +
  theme(text=element_text(family="Times New Roman", size=12), plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) + 
  labs(title = expression(paste("DynaMut2 ΔΔG vs. -Rosetta ΔΔG")),
       y = expression(paste(-Delta*Delta*G, " (kcal/mol, Rosetta)")),
       x = expression(paste(Delta*Delta*G, " (kcal/mol, DynaMut2)")),
       color= "Protein",
       fill="Protein") 

print(ddgs_scatterplot)
```

```{r}
# Study relationship between delta_tm and DDG using a linear mixed effects model
# Account for differing intercepts using protein as a random effect
rosetta_vs_dynamut <- lmerTest::lmer(dynamut2_prediction ~ ddG + (1|protein), data = mutations_df)

# Print model summary to check significance
summary(rosetta_vs_dynamut)
```

Both visual inspection and the linear mixed effects model seem to hint that the predictions show similar trends. However, as the predictions are classified as "stabilizing" and "destabilizing" using cutoffs, the tools do not always agree on the classification even if they exhibit linear relationship in their predictions. Let's check this with a confusion matrix: 

```{r}
# Add a column indicating Rosetta classification
mutations_df <- mutations_df %>%
  mutate(rosetta_classification = ifelse(ddG > 0, "Destabilizing", "Stabilizing"))

# Add a column indicating DynaMut2 classification
mutations_df <- mutations_df %>%
  mutate(dynamut2_classification = ifelse(dynamut2_prediction < 0, "Destabilizing", "Stabilizing"))

# Create a confusion matrix
confusion_mat <- confusionMatrix(data = factor(mutations_df$dynamut2_classification),
                                 reference = factor(mutations_df$rosetta_classification),
                                 positive = "Stabilizing")
# Print the confusion matrix
print(confusion_mat)
```
Based on the confusion matrix using a simplified cutoff for Rosetta CartesianDDG (excluding the neutral mutation category), the tools disagree on 12 of 51 mutations (where both predictions were present).

# Density plots of $\Delta T_m$, Rosetta $\Delta \Delta$G and DynaMut2 $\Delta \Delta$G

```{r, fig.align = 'center'}
# Create the density plot
max_density = max(max(density(mutations_df[mutations_df$protein == "Brazzein",]$delta_tm, na.rm=TRUE)$y), 
                  max(density(mutations_df[mutations_df$protein == "Thaumatin",]$delta_tm, na.rm=TRUE)$y), 
                  max(density(mutations_df[mutations_df$protein == "Monellin",]$delta_tm, na.rm=TRUE)$y))

y_max = max_density + 0.1*max_density
y_min = -0.2*max_density
box_width = 0.15*max_density
box_y = y_min - 0.5*y_min

densityplot <- ggplot(mutations_df, aes(x = delta_tm, y=box_y)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, aes(y=box_y), size=0.8) + 
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.5, aes(fill = protein), width=box_width, outlier.size=0.8) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5, aes(x = delta_tm, fill = protein), inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(y_min, y_max)) + 
  theme_light() +
  theme(text=element_text(family="Times New Roman", size=12), plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)) + 
  geom_vline(xintercept=0, alpha=0.5) +
  labs(x = expression(paste(Delta*T[m], " (\u00B0C)")), 
       y = "Density", 
       title = expression(paste("Density plot of ", Delta*T[m])), 
       fill = "Protein",
       color = "Protein") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = color_list, name = "Protein") +
  facet_grid(protein ~ .) +
  scale_fill_discrete()

print(densityplot)
```

```{r}
mutations_df$grantham_d <- ""
mutations_df$mut_exp_string <- ""
mutations_df$conservation <- ""

brazzein_conservation = read.csv("/Users/pqh443/Desktop/WP2 - sweet proteins/Kibby_results/Brazzein/conservation.csv")
monellin_conservation = read.csv("/Users/pqh443/Desktop/WP2 - sweet proteins/Kibby_results/Monellin/conservation.csv")
thaumatin_conservation = read.csv("/Users/pqh443/Desktop/WP2 - sweet proteins/Kibby_results/Thaumatin/conservation.csv")

brazzein_df = data.frame(strsplit(brazzein_conservation$conservation, " "))
colnames(brazzein_df) = "conservation"
brazzein_df$aminoacid = strsplit(brazzein_conservation$sequence, "")[[1]]
brazzein_df$position = row.names(brazzein_df)
brazzein_df$protein = "Brazzein"

thaumatin_df = data.frame(strsplit(thaumatin_conservation$conservation, " "))
colnames(thaumatin_df) = "conservation"
thaumatin_df$aminoacid = strsplit(thaumatin_conservation$sequence, "")[[1]]
thaumatin_df$position = row.names(thaumatin_df)
thaumatin_df$protein = "Thaumatin"

monellin_df = data.frame(strsplit(monellin_conservation$conservation, " "))
colnames(monellin_df) = "conservation"
monellin_df$aminoacid = strsplit(monellin_conservation$sequence, "")[[1]]
monellin_df$position = row.names(monellin_df)
monellin_df$protein = "Monellin"

conservation_scores = rbind(brazzein_df, monellin_df)
conservation_scores = rbind(conservation_scores, thaumatin_df)

conservation_scores$mutation = paste(conservation_scores$aminoacid, conservation_scores$position, sep ="")

mutations_df$conservation = as.numeric(mutations_df$conservation)

# Loop over the unique protein IDs
for (protein_id in unique(mutations_df$protein_id)) {
    mutations = mutations_df[mutations_df$protein_id == protein_id,]$mut_list
    protein = mutations_df[mutations_df$protein_id == protein_id,]$protein
    
    mutations_ls = strsplit(mutations," ")[[1]]
    
    grantham_distances = c()
    conservation_scs = c()
    mut_string_full = ""
    
    for (mut in mutations_ls){
      mut_AAs = (unlist(strsplit(mut, "\\d+")))
      position <- gsub("[^0-9]", "", mut)
      grantham_d = grantham_distance(as_three_letter(mut_AAs[1]), as_three_letter(mut_AAs[2]))[["d"]]
      mut_exp_string = paste(as_three_letter(mut_AAs[1]), position, as_three_letter(mut_AAs[2]), sep = "-")
      if (length(mutations_ls) > 1){
          mut_string_full = paste(mut_string_full, mut_exp_string, sep = ", ")
      } else {
          mut_string_full = mut_exp_string
      }
      
      orig_AA = paste(mut_AAs[1], position, sep = "")
      
      conservation_mut = as.numeric(conservation_scores[(conservation_scores$protein == protein & conservation_scores$mutation == orig_AA),]$conservation)
      conservation_scs = append(conservation_scs, conservation_mut)
      print(mean(conservation_scs))
      grantham_distances = append(grantham_distances, grantham_d)
    }

    mutations_df[mutations_df$protein_id == protein_id,]$conservation = mean(conservation_scs)
    mutations_df[mutations_df$protein_id == protein_id,]$grantham_d = mean(grantham_distances)
    mutations_df[mutations_df$protein_id == protein_id,]$mut_exp_string = sub(", ", "", mut_string_full)
}

```

```{r}
braz_cons = mutations_df[mutations_df$protein == "Brazzein",]$conservation
thau_cons = mutations_df[mutations_df$protein == "Thaumatin",]$conservation
mone_cons = mutations_df[mutations_df$protein == "Monellin",]$conservation

# Combine the three groups into a single list
conserv <- list(braz_cons, thau_cons, mone_cons)

# Perform the Kruskal-Wallis test
kruskal_result <- kruskal.test(conserv)

# Display the test result
print(kruskal_result)

# Perform post hoc tests (using Dunn's test) after Kruskal-Wallis
posthoc_results <- dunn.test(conserv)

# Display post hoc test results
print(posthoc_results)

mean(braz_cons)
mean(mone_cons)

```


```{r}
# Function to read AlphaFold2 models as a dataframe
read_alphafold_pdb <- function(file_path, model_name = NA){
  
  # Read the file line by line
  lines <- readLines(file_path)
  
  # Initialize an empty dataframe
  parsed_df <- data.frame()
  
  # Loop through the lines and process them
  for (line in lines) {
   
    if (startsWith(line, "ATOM")) {
      
      # Split the line using one or more spaces as the delimiter
      parsed_line <- str_split(line, '\\s+')
      
      # Remove empty elements
      parsed_line <- parsed_line[[1]][parsed_line[[1]] != ""]
      
      if(is.na(model_name)){
          # Set the name of the pdb files in the atom filed
          parsed_line[1] <- gsub("\\.pdb$", "", basename(file_path))

      } else {
          parsed_line[1] <- model_name
      }
      # Create a new row in the dataframe
      parsed_df <- rbind(parsed_df, parsed_line)
    }
  }
  
  # Rename columns
  colnames(parsed_df) <- c("Model", "SerialNumber", "AtomName", "ResName", "ChainID", "ResSeqN", "X", "Y", "Z", "Occupancy", "pLDDT", "Element")
  
  # Convert columns to numeric
  columns_to_convert = c("SerialNumber", "ResSeqN", "X", "Y", "Z", "Occupancy", "pLDDT")
  parsed_df[columns_to_convert] <- apply(parsed_df[columns_to_convert], 2, as.numeric)

  return(parsed_df)
}

```

read_resfile <- function(input_path){
  data = read.csv(input_path, sep=",")
  data$Variant = gsub("\\_res\\.txt$", "", basename(input_path))
  data$residue_index = data$residue_index + 1
  colnames(data) <- c("ResSeqN", "protA_resname", "protB_resname", "ES", "Model")
  return(data)
}

resfiles <- Sys.glob("Documents/PDA_analysis_results/*_res.txt")

  resfile_data <- rbind(resfile_data, read_resfile(file))

  ylim(c(0,100)) +

  scale_color_discrete(name = "Model") + # Set legend title
  scale_y_continuous(name="pLDDT", sec.axis=sec_axis(~./scaleFactor, name="Effective Strain")) + 
  theme_minimal()

```{r}
library(reticulate)

use_python("/Users/pqh443/anaconda3/bin/python")
pd <- import("pandas")

plot_msa <- function(feature_dict_path, title){

  # Open feature pickle using pandas
  feature_dict <- pd$read_pickle(feature_dict_path)
  
  # Read MSA into a dataframe
  msa <- data.frame(feature_dict$msa)
  
  # Compare the first row to all other rows
  seqid = msa - matrix(rep(as.numeric(msa[1,]), times = nrow(msa)), nrow=nrow(msa), ncol=ncol(msa), byrow= T)
  seqid = (seqid == 0)*1

  # Calculate identity of the sequences in MSA
  seqid <- rowMeans(seqid)
  seqid_sort <- order(seqid)
  non_gaps <- data.frame(msa != 21)
  non_gaps <- as.data.frame(lapply(non_gaps, as.numeric))
  non_gaps[non_gaps == 0] <- NA
  
  msa_df <- non_gaps[seqid_sort, ] * seqid[seqid_sort]
  
  # Create a data frame for the MSA
  msa_df <- as.data.frame(msa_df)
  rownames(msa_df) <- 1:nrow(msa_df)
  colnames(msa_df) <- 1:ncol(msa_df)
  
  msa_df$row <- rownames(msa_df)

  long_df <- pivot_longer(msa_df, cols = -row, names_to = "ColumnID", values_to = "Value")

  # Dataframe for plotting the line showing total number of aligned sequences
  # at each position
  line_df <- data.frame(colSums(non_gaps, na.rm = T))
  colnames(line_df) <- "y"
  line_df$x <- 1:length(line_df$y)
  
  colnames(long_df) <- c("y", "x", "value")
  
  long_df <- as.data.frame(lapply(long_df, as.numeric))
  
  p <- ggplot(long_df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = value, color = value)) +
      geom_raster() +
      geom_line(data=line_df, aes(x=x, y=y), fill = NA, color = "black", inherit.aes = FALSE, size= 0.25) +
      labs(x = "Position", y = "Sequences") +
      ggtitle(title) +
      theme(text=element_text(family="Times New Roman", size=12), 
            plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face ="bold"),
            axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"), 
            legend.key.height = unit(2.5, "cm"),
            legend.title = element_text(size = 12, angle = -90),
            legend.title.align = 0.6,
            legend.direction = "vertical",
            panel.border = element_rect(colour = "grey", fill=NA, size=0.5)) + 
      scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
      scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
      guides(fill=guide_colorbar(ticks.colour = NA, barwidth = 0.5, barheight = 18.5, title.position = "right")) +
      scale_fill_gradientn(colours = rainbow(7), na.value = "white", name = "Sequence identity to query", limits=c(0,1), breaks=c(0, 0.25,0.5, 0.75, 1))
  return(p)
}

plot_msa("/Users/pqh443/Documents/SweetProteinVariants/Thaumatin-II/features.pkl", "Thaumatin-II native (MSA)")

```

    seqid = msa - matrix(rep(as.numeric(msa[1,]), times = nrow(msa)), nrow=nrow(msa), ncol=ncol(msa), byrow= T)
    seqid = (seqid == 0)*1

    seqid <- rowMeans(seqid)
    seqid_sort <- order(seqid)
    non_gaps <- data.frame(msa != 21)

    non_gaps[non_gaps == 0] <- NA

    msa_df <- non_gaps[seqid_sort, ] * seqid[seqid_sort]
    msa_df <- msa_df[rowSums(is.na(msa_df)) < length(colnames(msa_df)), ] 

    # Create a data frame for the MSA
    msa_df <- as.data.frame(msa_df)

    colnames(line_df) <- "y"
    line_df$x <- 1:length(line_df$y)

    long_df <- as.data.frame(lapply(long_df, as.numeric))
    
    p <- ggplot(long_df, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = value, color = value)) +
        geom_raster() +
        geom_line(data=line_df, aes(x=x, y=y), fill = NA, color = "black", inherit.aes = FALSE, size= 0.25) +
        labs(x = "Position", y = "Sequences") +
        ggtitle(title) +
        theme(text=element_text(family="Times New Roman", size=12), 
              plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face ="bold"),
              axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"), 
              legend.key.height = unit(2.5, "cm"),
              legend.title = element_text(size = 12, angle = -90),
              legend.title.align = 0.6,

        scale_fill_gradientn(colours = rainbow(7), na.value = "white", name = "Sequence identity to query", limits=c(0,1), breaks=c(0, 0.25,0.5, 0.75, 1))
    ggsave(paste0(output_path, "/", "MSA_", id, ".png"), p)
    }
